clue.text: Free rendering of a series of notes by the literary section

indicators.note: by means beside, so the section stands next to the notes

parts.note: PARA is short for paragraph, a section of written text
in music a phrase is a short run of notes heard as a unit

explanation.surface: A loose translation is made of a passage of music beside a bit of prose.
explanation.definitionFit: A paraphrase restates a text in other words, a loose version rather than a literal one.

clue.text: Hoffmann boy was under shock

parts.note: Heinrich Hoffmann's children's book ... is known in English as Shock-headed ..., the boy beneath a wild shock of hair

explanation.surface: A boy in Hoffmann's tale was badly shaken.
explanation.walkthrough: Shock seems to mean a fright, but it is a mop of hair: Hoffmann's Struwwelpeter, Shock-headed Peter.
explanation.definitionFit: Struwwelpeter's title character has a German name equivalent to the English given name in the grid.

clue.text: Opera sounds sanguinary

indicators.note: sounds says the words for bloody are said aloud to give the title

parts.note: sanguinary means bloody, here ruddy gore, red blood

explanation.surface: An opera that sounds bloodthirsty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sounds' says RUDDY GORE is said aloud; this is a Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera.
explanation.definitionFit: A Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera of 1887, the title of which is a play on bloodshed.

clue.text: Seemly part of Cocker's work?

parts.note: proper means seemly, decent
a fraction is a part of a whole

explanation.surface: A decent excerpt from a singer's work, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: Cocker suggests a singer; Edward Cocker wrote a famous 17th-century arithmetic book, hence the British phrase according to Cocker.
explanation.definitionFit: A fraction smaller than one is an example of the arithmetic Cocker taught.

clue.text: Dramatist was a queer sort also

indicators.note: queer means odd, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: and means also

explanation.surface: A playwright was an odd sort, too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'queer' rearranges SORT into ROST; Edmond Rostand wrote Cyrano de Bergerac.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmond Rostand was a French playwright, author of Cyrano de Bergerac.

clue.text: Time we got in a corner?

explanation.surface: Time that we spent cornered.
explanation.walkthrough: In boxing, the seconds are the helpers waiting in a fighter's corner.
explanation.definitionFit: Units of time a sixtieth of a minute; and a boxer's assistants who attend in the corner between rounds.

clue.text: LSD needed for this journey?

parts.note: LSD reads as old British money (pounds, shillings, pence) for a fare, but the drug gives a hallucinatory outing

explanation.surface: Someone asks how much cash a journey will cost.
explanation.walkthrough: LSD was the abbreviation for pre-decimal British money, so the clue seems to ask about a fare; the drug LSD gives a different sort of journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a hallucinogenic drug experience is a kind of journey of the mind.

clue.text: Rule some umpire ignored

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A rule the umpire chose to overlook.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch's reign is the period of their rule.

clue.text: Birds seen by countrymen round Hindhead

indicators.note: round says the countrymen surround the other letter

parts.note: peasants are country people
the head, or first letter, of hind

explanation.surface: Game birds spotted by locals around a Surrey village.
explanation.walkthrough: Hindhead is a Surrey village, but read as hind head it is H; 'round' puts PEASANTS round H.
explanation.definitionFit: Pheasants are long-tailed game birds.

clue.text: Where the queen was calm Albert also, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals that these letters may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Queen Victoria was at peace, and her husband Albert too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges CALM ALBERT ALSO; Victoria and Albert bought this Scottish royal residence.
explanation.definitionFit: The royal family's Scottish estate on Deeside is where the monarch stays in summer.

clue.text: Boring duties nothing varied

indicators.note: varied means changed about, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Dull chores with no variety at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'varied' asks for DUTIES plus O to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tedious is wearisome and dull, the same as boring.

clue.text: Cup presented by church woman

parts.note: Alice stands for any woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman of the parish donates a cup.
explanation.walkthrough: The page breaks the line after church, so church and woman are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A chalice is a goblet, especially the one used for communion wine.

clue.text: Make a great fuss, as first mate had to do

definitions.text: as first mate had to do

explanation.surface: Someone causes a scene, as a ship's first mate must.
explanation.walkthrough: First mate suggests a ship's officer, but it means Adam and Eve, the first couple, whose son was Cain.
explanation.definitionFit: To create an uproar is an idiom; and Adam and Eve literally brought up their son Cain.

clue.text: Less dash, perhaps

explanation.surface: Less of a dash, maybe.
explanation.definitionFit: Five less two uses the word for subtraction; and the subtraction sign is a short horizontal stroke.

clue.text: Evidence might be corrected?

explanation.surface: Proof that the evidence could be put right.
explanation.definitionFit: Evidence that establishes a fact; and a printer's trial sheet is marked up by the editor.

clue.text: Plan of action available to theatre-goers

explanation.surface: A plan sold at the theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A schedule of intended activities; and the booklet listing cast and details sold at a play.

clue.text: Abandoning demand for rise, noted bewilderment

indicators.note: bewilderment is confusion, so these letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Walking out on a pay claim, the clerk was baffled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bewilderment' asks for RISE and NOTED to be rearranged; 'demand for' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Desertion is the act of forsaking a post or person, which is abandoning them.

clue.text: It's encouraging to get in the money I've needed

parts.note: a cent is a coin, a unit of money

explanation.surface: Getting paid is a motivation.
explanation.definitionFit: An inducement or spur that motivates someone is something that encourages.

clue.text: Appeared as Hamlet without permit?

parts.note: read as performing without a licence, but really playing the prince too hammily, beyond what is permitted on stage

explanation.surface: An actor played Hamlet in an unlicensed show.
explanation.walkthrough: Without permit reads as unlicensed; it means beyond what is allowed, playing a part too broadly.
explanation.definitionFit: To ham a role is to perform it with exaggeration, beyond the bounds of restraint.

clue.text: Retires from Navy in Tunis, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals that these letters may be arranged another way

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A sailor leaves the fleet while stationed in Tunisia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges RN with TUNIS.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn in is an idiom for going to bed, as retires means.

clue.text: How to land balloon, even in the river

indicators.note: in places the word for even inside the river

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain
flat means even, level

explanation.surface: A balloonist lands on level ground by the river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dee is one of several British rivers of that name; a balloonist lets the gas out to come down.
explanation.definitionFit: Letting the gas out of a balloon brings it down to earth.

clue.text: See copper's place

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper, plus the S of the possessive

explanation.surface: Look at the policeman's house.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper suggests a British policeman; it is the metal, Cu.
explanation.definitionFit: Locus is Latin for a position or site, used in English for a place.

clue.text: Just the outfit to take the voltage

parts.note: a rig is an outfit of clothes or equipment
HT stands for high tension, a high voltage

explanation.surface: Just the kit needed to handle the electrical supply.
explanation.definitionFit: Right and just both mean fair or morally correct.

clue.text: Group of African antelopes going round east

indicators.note: going round says the antelopes surround the other letter

parts.note: gnus are wildebeest, African antelopes
E is east

explanation.surface: A herd of antelopes circling to the east.
explanation.definitionFit: In biology a genus is a class of related species.

clue.text: Forbore to put painter in cultured surroundings

indicators.note: in ... surroundings places one piece within the other

parts.note: refined means cultured, polished in manners
RA is a Royal Academician, a painter

explanation.surface: Someone held back from setting an artist in a sophisticated milieu.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, for Royal Academician, is the crossword's usual painter.
explanation.definitionFit: To forbear is to hold back from doing something, the meaning of refrained.

clue.text: Figure how to develop a plot?

explanation.surface: A gardener's figure for working a plot.
explanation.definitionFit: A numeral from nought to nine; and turning soil over is how a garden plot is worked.

clue.text: Asians make Scotsman hit back

parts.note: mon is a Scots form of man, used as a word for a Scotsman

indicators.note: back says the word for hit is read from right to left

parts.note: slog means hit hard

explanation.surface: Some Asians get a Scot to hit back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses SLOG to give GOLS.
explanation.definitionFit: Mongols are a people of central Asia.

clue.text: A number object to join Iceland's parliament

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
a thing is an object

explanation.surface: A certain number object to joining Iceland's parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: The Althing is the national assembly of Iceland, among the oldest legislatures.

clue.text: Milton's harmonious sister is against such language

indicators.note: is says the sister's name equals against plus the language, so removing the against letter leaves the language

parts.note: in Milton's At a Solemn Music, Voice and Verse are the sphere-born harmonious sisters
V is short for versus, meaning against

explanation.surface: Milton's musical sister objects to this tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: VERSE is read as V (against) plus the answer, so taking V away leaves it.
explanation.definitionFit: Erse is an old name for the Gaelic language of Scotland or Ireland.

clue.text: Prior backed mount — church tend to get upset

indicators.note: backed says the name of the mount is read from right to left

parts.note: Etna is a volcano, a mount in Sicily
CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A monastery prior backs up the mountain while churchgoers grow annoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns ETNA into ANTE; 'to get upset' turns TEND into DENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Antecedent means coming before in time, just as prior does.
